correctness.rationale: For a fixed position \(i\), occurrences of \(1^r\) are exactly the final \(2^i\) residues in a period of length \(2^{i+r}\). The resulting summand has the explicit floor-plus-tail formula in RESULT.md. A complete residue case split proves that summand superadditive for arbitrary inputs; the total block count is a finite sum of those summands. The equality strip follows directly by prefixing a leading \(1\) and locating the unique possible new boundary occurrence. The verifier independently compares direct string counts to the formula, tests more than a million input pairs, checks residue boundaries, and replays the equality strip. Finite computation is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The finding directly answers the concrete \(11\)-block example in a published questions section and extends it to every all-one block \(1^r\), so the parameter family is mathematically motivated rather than an arbitrary slice. The dyadic equality strip also determines the sharp qualitative form of any Graham-style correction: unlike the digit-sum inequality, no positive correction depending only on the smaller addend can hold. This structural contrast is useful for future attempts to classify which block-counting functions admit additive inequalities.
